# Halves and quarters {#sec-periods} Targets: each team's points in 1H, 2H (with OT), and Q1–Q4 (regulation). A natural decomposition: $$ \text{points}_{p} \;\approx\; \text{exp\_points} \times \text{share}_p, $$ where $\text{share}_p$ is the fraction of a team's points scored in period $p$. Two versions of the share were tried: the **league's** share, and each team's own **as-of** share (exponentially weighted over prior games, blended with the share the opponent's defense usually allows). The final model uses the league share as its base, with LightGBM correcting the residual. ## Accuracy by period ::: {#tbl-periods .cell tbl-cap='Walk-forward CV MAE (points per team, 2019–2023) by period.' execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
mean points constant exp × league share exp × team share model model vs constant %
period
1H 14.36 7.42 6.66 6.68 6.56 -11.60
2H 13.51 6.78 6.35 6.42 6.29 -7.23
Q1 6.18 4.51 4.34 4.39 4.28 -5.23
Q2 8.18 5.25 4.90 4.94 4.83 -7.99
Q3 6.28 4.55 4.39 4.44 4.30 -5.46
Q4 6.94 4.46 4.58 4.64 4.45 -0.21
``` ::: ::: - The model beats the constant in every period, by about 12% in 1H and very little in Q4. - **Team-specific scoring shares are worse than the league share.** How a team splits its points across quarters is mostly noise, and it regresses to the league pattern. - **Q4 is special**: expected points × share does *worse* than a constant. ## Game script: why Q4 doesn't follow team strength ::: {.cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Share of a team's regulation points scored in Q4, by the team's expected margin (2019–2023).](periods_files/figure-pdf/fig-game-script-output-1.pdf){#fig-game-script} ::: ::: Big favorites score only about a fifth of their points in Q4: they run the clock once the game is decided. Big underdogs score close to 30% there (garbage time). Q4 points barely grow with team strength, unlike Q1–Q3. It's a nonlinear effect of one variable (expected margin), and trees capture it directly. ## Medians, not means The period models train on absolute error, so each prediction is the period's **median**. That's the right number for an over/under (the 50/50 point), but medians don't add up: quarter predictions sum below the full-game prediction, because quarters have many zeros and a right skew. The periods aren't meant to reconcile exactly. **Status:** accuracy only. There are no period betting lines yet; see @sec-roadmap for the options and costs.
